title: JavaScript Core Concepts
description: Essential JS concepts every developer should know

cards.back: A function that retains access to its outer scope even after the outer function returns
var: function-scoped, hoisted. let: block-scoped. const: block-scoped, no reassignment
Variable/function declarations are moved to the top of their scope before code executes
A mechanism that processes the call stack and callback queue, enabling async JS in a single thread
all: rejects on first failure. allSettled: waits for all, never rejects
A function that always returns the same output for the same inputs and has no side effects
==: type coercion (loose equality). ===: no coercion (strict equality)

cards.front: What is 'this' in an arrow function?
cards.back: Arrow functions don't have their own 'this' — they inherit it from the enclosing lexical scope
Objects inherit properties from other objects via the prototype chain, not classes
Expands an iterable (array/object) into individual elements. Used for copy, merge, rest params
undefined: variable declared but not assigned. null: intentional absence of value
Caching function results so repeated calls with the same args return instantly
async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises — makes async code look synchronous
Delaying a function call until after a period of inactivity (e.g. search input)
Ensuring a function is called at most once per time interval
